question: What is the big downside of using a simple flat daily rate (per diem) to cost nursing care?

options.A: it is illegal to use in modern public hospitals
options.B: It ignores individual patient needs and care complexity
options.C: It only calculates the cost of surgical procedures
options.D: It requires complex computer software for every shift

explanation: A flat daily rate assumes every single patient costs the same to nurse, which isn't fair because a critical patient needs way more work than someone resting comfortably.

question: What is the main job of the posterior pituitary gland?

options.A: It breaks down worn-out hormones in the bloodstream
options.B: It stores and releases hormones produced by the hypothalamus
options.C: It manufactures tropic hormones for the adrenal glands
options.D: It controls blood calcium levels using direct neural input

explanation: The posterior pituitary acts like a warehouse—it doesn't make hormones itself, but safely stores and releases them when needed.

question: What is the main purpose of milieu therapy on a psychiatric ward?

options.A: Creating a safe and therapeutic environment for recovery
options.B: Reducing the cost of hospital building maintenance
options.C: Isolating disruptive patients from the general public
options.D: Testing new experimental pharmaceutical products

explanation: Milieu therapy uses the physical layout and daily social interactions on the ward to create a secure, structured space where healing can happen.

question: How long does the post-natal period (puerperium) typically last in clinical practice?

options.A: Six months
options.B: Two weeks
options.C: Six weeks
options.D: Three months

explanation: You'll see this time and again in midwifery! The post-natal period is officially defined as the first six weeks after childbirth when the mother's body returns to its pre-pregnant state.

question: Which group makes up most of the residents in long-term care facilities?

options.A: Adults admitted strictly for acute post-surgical wound care
options.B: Children with congenital respiratory complications
options.C: Younger adults recovering from short-term sports injuries
options.D: Older adults with multiple chronic illnesses and frailty

explanation: Spot on! Older adults make up the majority of long-term care residents because aging often brings multiple health needs that require daily support.

question: Why must you write down any recent antibiotics the patient is taking on the lab request form?

options.A: The laboratory requires proof that the prescription was filled
options.B: Medications can affect microbial growth and test interpretation
options.C: Pharmacies will not process the sample without this record
options.D: It determines the financial cost billed to the patient

explanation: Antibiotics in the patient's system can stop germs from growing in the lab dish, so the lab needs to know so they don't misread a false negative!

question: What is the leading underlying medical condition that weakens bones and causes low-impact fractures?

options.A: Osteoarthritis
options.B: Atherosclerosis
options.C: Hypertension
options.D: Osteoporosis

explanation: Osteoporosis reduces bone mass and density, making the skeleton fragile and prone to breaking from minor bumps or normal daily activities. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h4)

question: Why is equitable distribution of funds across urban and rural clinics important?

options.A: To prevent rural health collapse and ensure all citizens have access to basic care
options.B: To make sure city hospitals get all the newest vehicles
options.C: To reduce the number of nurses working in rural areas
options.D: To satisfy international organizations without helping patients

explanation: Fair funding stops the concentration of resources only in cities while villages suffer without medicines. [learn more](GST322_U4_T2#GST322_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why do we usually draw blood cultures from two different sites?

options.A: To reduce the pain experienced in one single arm
options.B: To help distinguish true infection from skin contamination
options.C: To speed up the laboratory processing time significantly
options.D: To collect a larger total volume of blood for testing

explanation: Drawing from two spots helps us know if bacteria in the bottle came from the patient's bloodstream or just from the skin during the poke.

question: What is the primary maternal function of human chorionic gonadotropin in early pregnancy?

options.A: To stimulate milk production in maternal breast tissue
options.B: To lower maternal blood pressure for fetal protection
options.C: To trigger the immediate onset of active labour contractions
options.D: To stimulate the corpus luteum to produce progesterone

explanation: hCG signals the corpus luteum to keep producing progesterone early on, which protects and maintains the uterine lining until the placenta can take over that job. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h1)

question: Why should families pick a specific meeting place outside their home when planning for emergencies?

options.A: To ensure everyone can reunite safely if separated during an evacuation
options.B: To provide a storage space for heavy rescue tools
options.C: To serve as a temporary community clinic
options.D: To give neighbors a place to park their vehicles

explanation: Brilliant! Having a pre-arranged meeting spot saves precious time and stops panic if family members get separated during a sudden crisis.

question: What does checking a client's orientation involve during a mental status check?

options.A: Measuring the daily fluid intake and output
options.B: Testing physical muscle strength in the legs
options.C: Asking about person, place, and time
options.D: Checking hearing ability with a tuning fork

explanation: Orientation checks confirm if the client knows who they are, where they are located, and what time or date it is. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h4)

question: Who is primarily responsible for creating strategic plans in a healthcare organization?

options.A: Patient care assistants
options.B: Top-tier nursing executives
options.C: Shift charge nurses
options.D: Bedside staff nurses

explanation: Strategic plans are high-level organization-wide goals created by top leaders like the Director of Nursing or Chief Nursing Officer. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is the biggest perk of giving chemotherapy drugs through the intraperitoneal route?

options.A: It delivers a high concentration of the drug directly to abdominal tumors
options.B: It allows the liver to break down the medicine before it works
options.C: It makes the drug absorb instantly into the brain tissue
options.D: It completely prevents the drug from ever reaching the bloodstream

explanation: Brilliant! By putting chemo straight into the belly, you give the tumor a powerful, direct bath of medicine right where it lives. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h3)

question: How can nurse burnout negatively affect counselling sessions?

options.A: It automatically increases clinic funding
options.B: It reduces the nurse's ability to show empathy
options.C: It removes all language barriers in the room
options.D: It improves the speed of patient discharges

explanation: When you're exhausted and burnt out, it's so much harder to find the emotional energy to deeply connect with your patients. Take care of yourselves, future nurses!

question: What does a 'cycloplegic' drug do when dropped into the eye?

options.A: Increases the drainage of fluid from the eye chambers
options.B: Constricts the pupil down to a tiny pinpoint size
options.C: Numbs the surface of the cornea for a quick check
options.D: Paralyzes the focusing muscle inside the eye

explanation: Cycloplegics put the ciliary muscle on pause so it can't focus. This is super helpful during eye exams or surgeries when the eye needs to stay completely relaxed.

question: When is a nurse most likely to initiate intravenous therapy for a patient?

options.A: When the patient needs a rapid correction of severe dehydration.
options.B: When the patient is eating normally and taking daily multivitamin pills.
options.C: When topical skin cream is prescribed for a localized rash.
options.D: When a mild headache needs to be relieved over an eight-hour period.

explanation: Severe dehydration requires quick fluid volume restoration directly into the blood vessels, which can only be achieved effectively through IV therapy. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h1)

question: What is a key duty of a nurse acting as a facilitator in a community?

options.A: Punishing community members who refuse to take their medications
options.B: Demanding immediate resignation of corrupt hospital directors
options.C: Writing new national health laws without community input
options.D: Connecting marginalized groups with health resources and social programs

explanation: Spot on! As a facilitator, your job is to bridge the gap—connecting people who need help with the exact services and agencies that can provide it.

question: A hospital is introducing a new electronic health record system. Who is most likely responsible for training the bedside nursing staff on how to use it?

options.A: The head pharmacist
options.B: The biomedical equipment technician
options.C: The hospital chief executive officer
options.D: The nursing informaticist

explanation: Training staff on new clinical documentation systems falls directly under the educational and implementation duties of a nursing informaticist. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h4)

question: In Nigeria, what do we mean by the 'double burden of disease'?

options.A: Having two different types of cancer simultaneously in one organ
options.B: Paying double taxes for healthcare services in public and private hospitals
options.C: Dealing with both infectious diseases and non-communicable diseases at the same time
options.D: Experiencing high rates of both malaria and severe malnutrition

explanation: Spot on! The double burden means our communities are fighting traditional infectious diseases (like malaria) while also seeing a sharp rise in chronic illnesses (like hypertension and diabetes).

question: What is the main reason for filling out an incident report after an adverse drug reaction?

options.A: To punish the nurse who gave the drug
options.B: To calculate the cost of the emergency treatment
options.C: To track safety data and prevent future drug reactions
options.D: To discharge the patient from the ward

explanation: Incident reports aren't for punishment—they help the hospital learn, improve safety, and protect future patients from the same mistake.

question: What is the main purpose of taking a nutrition history in nursing practice?

options.A: To gather information about a patient's food intake and eating habits
options.B: To strictly calculate the exact daily financial cost of groceries
options.C: To diagnose rare genetic metabolic disorders immediately
options.D: To prescribe specific medical diets without consulting a doctor

explanation: A nutrition history focuses directly on understanding what and how a patient eats to guide their care. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h1)

question: What classic mix of symptoms do you expect to see in an opioid overdose?

options.A: Rapid heart rate, muscle tremors, and agitation
options.B: Profuse sweating, diarrhea, and high blood pressure
options.C: High fever, dry skin, and wide pupils
options.D: Slow breathing, extreme sleepiness, and pinpoint pupils

explanation: Picture a sleeping patient who is breathing very slowly with tiny, pin-point pupils—that's the classic classic opioid sign you'll learn to spot instantly!

question: Which facility type represents the primary level of healthcare delivery?

options.A: Federal medical centre
options.B: Primary health care centre
options.C: Specialized surgical clinic
options.D: Teaching hospital

explanation: Primary health care centres and health posts form the grassroots level where basic family planning services are first accessed. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h3)

question: Why are corticosteroids sometimes given along with antibiotics for bacterial meningitis?

options.A: To help antibiotics break down cell walls faster
options.B: To calm down inflammation and lower the risk of lasting damage like hearing loss
options.C: To replace the need for intravenous fluids
options.D: To numb the back so the patient feels no pain during procedures

explanation: When antibiotics suddenly kill millions of bacteria, the body's immune reaction can cause a massive wave of inflammation. Steroids help calm that swelling down so it doesn't harm the brain or hearing.

question: How do NGOs commonly help out rural health posts?

options.A: Writing national tax laws for health
options.B: Importing luxury vehicles for officials
options.C: Supplying essential drugs and medical equipment
options.D: Owning and operating commercial banks

explanation: You're right! NGOs frequently step in to provide the actual medicines and basic tools that rural clinics are missing. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h3)

question: Why is documentation in home health care uniquely different from hospital documentation?

options.A: Home records are only reviewed by the client and never by other clinicians
options.B: Home records do not require dates or signatures from the attending nurse
options.C: Home records account for environmental and family dynamics in the living space
options.D: Home records are legally binding only if written in pencil

explanation: Home care takes place where people live, so records must capture household conditions and family support systems that affect recovery. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why is a woman's fertile window wider than just the single day she ovulates?

options.A: Eggs can remain fertile in the fallopian tubes for nearly a week.
options.B: Sperm can survive inside the female reproductive tract for up to five days.
options.C: Hormones remain elevated for a full week after ovulation.
options.D: Multiple eggs are released over several days during every cycle.

explanation: Sperm are remarkably resilient! Because they can hang out in the female tract for up to five days, intercourse days before ovulation can still lead to pregnancy.

question: What causes the Mazzotti reaction when treating an onchocerciasis patient?

options.A: The rapid immune reaction to dying microfilariae
options.B: Complete failure of the patient's liver and kidneys
options.C: Bacterial superinfection in the skin snip sites
options.D: A direct toxic allergic reaction to the drug capsule

explanation: When ivermectin kills thousands of microfilariae all at once, the sudden immune system cleanup causes fever, rash, and swelling known as the Mazzotti reaction.

question: Why is Family Life Education an important part of primary health care?

options.A: It eliminates all infectious diseases from the community
options.B: It guarantees financial stability for every household
options.C: It completely replaces the need for hospital-based doctors
options.D: It equips individuals with knowledge to make healthy life choices

explanation: When people get the right information about their bodies and relationships, they can make smart choices to protect their health!

question: What is the main goal of the fluid released by the bulbourethral glands?

options.A: To stimulate testosterone production
options.B: To form the hard outer shell of semen
options.C: To provide primary nutrition for sperm
options.D: To neutralize acid in the urethra

explanation: Since urine is acidic and passes through the same tube, the bulbourethral glands send out a clear mucus to clean and neutralize the path right before ejaculation.

question: What is the best approach when advising a pregnant mum on a tight budget about her diet?

options.A: Insisting that she must purchase organic foods to have a healthy baby
options.B: Suggesting affordable, locally available food alternatives that meet her nutritional needs
options.C: Skipping dietary counseling because poverty makes nutrition impossible to change
options.D: Telling her to buy expensive imported supplements from specialized pharmacies

explanation: Great nursing care is practical and real! Always guide patients toward nourishing, budget-friendly local foods they can actually access.

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical duty of a nurse working in a community mental health center?

options.A: Administering long-acting injectable psychiatric medications
options.B: Performing major neurosurgery for treatment-resistant depression
options.C: Connecting vulnerable clients with local housing and food resources
options.D: Providing psychoeducation to patients and their family members

explanation: Nurses in community settings do not perform neurosurgery; their role focuses on support, education, medication management, and resource linkage. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h7)

question: What happens to maternal bones if a breastfeeding mother does not consume enough calcium in her diet?

options.A: Her bones become significantly denser and stronger
options.B: Calcium is drawn from her bones to maintain milk quality
options.C: Her body stops producing milk until she takes supplements
options.D: Her breast milk becomes completely devoid of calcium

explanation: The body will take calcium from the mother's bones to ensure the baby's milk has what it needs if dietary intake falls short. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h4)

question: A woman with a history of Type III FGM is admitted in labor. What complication should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Obstructed labor and severe perineal tearing
options.B: Rapid, painless delivery with zero complications
options.C: Complete absence of uterine contractions
options.D: Immediate spontaneous rupture of membranes without pain

explanation: Correct! The heavy scar tissue and tight narrowing from Type III FGM can block the birth canal, leading to a difficult delivery unless carefully managed.

question: A clinic ensures that all adolescents receive care regardless of their financial status or background. Which core principle does this practice demonstrate?

options.A: Acceptability
options.B: Appropriateness
options.C: Confidentiality
options.D: Equitability

explanation: Equitability means treating all young clients fairly without discrimination based on status, gender, or ability to pay. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h2)

question: Why is checking out the home environment so important for a patient's nutrition?

options.A: It guarantees the patient will eat all prescribed meals
options.B: It reveals practical barriers like trouble with grocery shopping
options.C: It proves whether the family is hiding food from the patient
options.D: It replaces the need to check the patient's weight

explanation: Exactly! Home visits show you real-life challenges, like physical issues that make buying or cooking food hard.

question: You get a tray of washed surgical scissors and spot dried blood stuck in the hinges. What's your next move?

options.A: Send the tray back to decontamination for re-cleaning
options.B: Place the tray directly into the warm incubator
options.C: Wipe the outside surfaces with alcohol swabs
options.D: Proceed with wrapping and sterilization anyway

explanation: Never wrap a dirty instrument! Any leftover blood or gunk will protect germs from the sterilizing heat, so back to the sink it goes.

question: How does expressive aphasia usually show up in a stroke patient?

options.A: Severe shaking of the hands during writing
options.B: Inability to hear sound waves entering the ear
options.C: Total blindness in both visual fields
options.D: Difficulty speaking or finding the right words to say

explanation: With expressive aphasia, the patient usually understands what you're saying, but struggles to get their own words out. Patience is key!

question: How does knowledge happen when using intuition?

options.A: By reading old medical journals in the hospital library
options.B: Through strict adherence to hospital procedure manuals
options.C: By performing a double-blind randomized clinical trial
options.D: Through an immediate gut feeling or hunch without conscious reasoning

explanation: Intuition skips the slow steps of logic and gives you a sudden inner sense that something is right (or wrong).

question: Why are balancing measures important when implementing a new nursing procedure?

options.A: They help detect unintended side effects or new problems in other areas of care
options.B: They calculate the exact financial profit generated by the new nursing intervention
options.C: They replace the need for measuring patient outcomes
options.D: They ensure that every single staff member agrees with the new policy

explanation: Exactly! Fixing one thing can sometimes accidentally cause a problem elsewhere. Balancing measures help us catch those side effects early.

question: A patient vomits severely just two hours after eating leftover rice. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Primary viral lung infection
options.B: Food-borne intoxication
options.C: Parasitic bowel infestation
options.D: Chronic autoimmune reaction

explanation: Spot on! That super-short window between eating and vomiting is the classic signature of a food toxin (intoxication). Keep up the fantastic work!

question: What is the main purpose of a tactical plan in a healthcare setting?

options.A: To break strategic goals down into medium-term steps
options.B: To replace the need for long-term organizational visions
options.C: To punish staff who fail to meet quotas
options.D: To dictate minute-by-minute patient care tasks

explanation: Tactical plans take big organizational goals and turn them into concrete, achievable projects for specific departments over a couple of years. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why does a severe opioid overdose lead to dangerous breathing problems?

options.A: It causes immediate physical swelling and closure of the main vocal cords
options.B: It depresses the respiratory control center in the brainstem, reducing breathing rate
options.C: It freezes the movement of the diaphragm muscle by destroying motor nerves
options.D: It triggers severe allergic bronchospasm in the small bronchial airways

explanation: Opioids affect the part of the brain that tells the body to breathe, causing breathing to slow down and eventually stop if untreated.

question: When a nurse visits a family's home to care for an infant, why is it helpful to view yourself as a 'guest'?

options.A: To respect the family's home environment and autonomy
options.B: To prevent the nurse from providing direct physical care
options.C: Because family members must supervise every nursing task
options.D: Because home nurses have fewer legal responsibilities

explanation: You got it! Walking into someone's home means respecting their private space, culture, and routines. It's the best way to build real trust.

question: What does 'social desirability bias' mean when assessing a patient's diet?

options.A: Reporting healthier eating habits to please the healthcare provider
options.B: Refusing to eat hospital meals due to cultural beliefs
options.C: Forgetting to log snacks and sugary beverages during the day
options.D: Failing to understand how to use a standard food scale

explanation: Patients want to impress us! They sometimes claim they eat better than they actually do just to please their nurse.

question: How does skeletal traction differ fundamentally from skin traction?

options.A: Skeletal traction avoids any risk of infection because no hardware is used
options.B: Skeletal traction uses much lighter weights for short periods
options.C: Skeletal traction attaches directly to bone using metal pins
options.D: Skeletal traction relies entirely on elastic bandages wrapped loosely

explanation: Skeletal traction requires surgical insertion of pins or wires into the bone to handle heavier weights over a longer duration, unlike skin-surface methods. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T7#GNS221_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which group of people often shows trauma through behavioral regression like bedwetting?

options.A: Trained rescue workers
options.B: Pregnant women
options.C: Elderly adults
options.D: Children

explanation: Children frequently lack the verbal capacity to describe their fear, so they express trauma through regressive behaviors. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h4)

question: What exactly is water pollution?

options.A: The natural filtration of rainwater through soil layers
options.B: The contamination of water sources by harmful substances
options.C: The evaporation of clean water from surface reservoirs
options.D: The normal movement of minerals from rocks into rivers

explanation: Spot on! Water pollution happens when harmful agents find their way into natural water bodies, making them unsafe for use.

question: Why do doctors frequently prescribe diuretics (water pills) for patients with Acute Glomerulonephritis?

options.A: To permanently cure the underlying bacterial infection
options.B: To stimulate a massive increase in red blood cell production
options.C: To reduce fluid overload and swelling
options.D: To lower the patient's body temperature during fever

explanation: Diuretics help the kidneys push out extra water and salt, which quickly brings down swelling and lowers dangerous blood pressure. Excellent nursing pharmacology!

question: What crucial warning must you give a patient prescribed benzonatate capsules?

options.A: Swallow the capsules whole without chewing.
options.B: Crush the pills and mix them into fruit juice.
options.C: Dissolve the capsule slowly on top of the tongue.
options.D: Open the capsule and rub the liquid on the throat.

explanation: Never let patients chew benzonatate! It will numb their mouth and throat so fast that they risk choking or aspiration.

question: Why is catching maternal distress early so important for a mum in labour?

options.A: It guarantees the avoidance of a Caesarean section
options.B: It prevents prolonged exhaustion and stalled labour progress
options.C: It stops the production of amniotic fluid completely
options.D: It eliminates the need for any pain relief medication

explanation: Great job! Catching distress early breaks the cycle of stress hormones, helping her contractions stay strong and keeping her labour moving forward.

question: What do we mean by 'out-of-pocket' spending in healthcare?

options.A: Direct cash payments made by patients at the point of service
options.B: Free medical supplies provided by international donor agencies
options.C: Monthly taxes collected automatically by the federal government
options.D: Reimbursements paid to nurses for working night shifts

explanation: Out-of-pocket simply means the patient is dipping straight into their own wallet to pay cash for care because there is no insurance.

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand water microbiology?

options.A: To help trace disease outbreaks and educate communities
options.B: To measure the exact depth of local rivers
options.C: To design large municipal water treatment plants
options.D: To chemically synthesize new antibiotics for hospitals

explanation: Nurses need this knowledge to connect water sources to community illnesses and teach safe hygiene habits. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h1)

question: Standard X-rays are most helpful for looking at which part of the body?

options.A: Ligaments and joint capsules
options.B: Skeletal muscles and tendons
options.C: Cortical and cancellous bone
options.D: Peripheral nerves and blood vessels

explanation: X-rays pass right through soft tissues, but dense bone blocks them. That makes a standard X-ray the go-to tool for spotting fractures and checking bone structure.

question: When should a nurse consider referring a psychiatric client to a sheltered workshop?

options.A: When the client is experiencing an acute, violent psychotic episode
options.B: When the client is medically stable but lacks skills for open jobs
options.C: When the client refuses to take any prescribed medications
options.D: When the client demands discharge against medical advice

explanation: Referral works best when acute symptoms are well-managed and the client is ready for gentle rehabilitation. Excellent nursing judgment!

question: A patient asks why eating soluble fiber helps protect their heart. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Fiber burns off extra calories before they turn into body fat
options.B: Fiber binds to cholesterol in your digestive tract so your body removes it
options.C: Fiber directly opens up tight blood vessels to improve circulation
options.D: Fiber replaces all the salt in your meals so your kidneys can rest

explanation: Soluble fiber binds with cholesterol-containing bile acids in the intestine, preventing their reabsorption and promoting their excretion in stool. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h3)

question: As a nurse, which non-clinical duty do you often perform in financed health systems?

options.A: Managing the national treasury accounts
options.B: Explaining insurance coverage and benefits to patients
options.C: Collecting taxes from local business owners
options.D: Setting the annual interest rates for community loans

explanation: Nurses are great educators! You will often help bridge the gap by explaining complex health programs in plain language patients can easily understand.

question: Which of these is NOT a job of the ordinary sweat glands (eccrine glands)?

options.A: Excreting tiny amounts of body waste
options.B: Producing thick, smelly sweat in the armpits
options.C: Helping cool down the body through sweat evaporation
options.D: Releasing watery fluid onto the skin

explanation: Spot on! Armpit and groin sweat comes from apocrine glands, while your ordinary (eccrine) glands make watery sweat all over to keep you cool. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h5)

question: What do we call an unexpected injury caused by medical care rather than the patient's actual sickness?

options.A: Latent condition
options.B: Near miss
options.C: Sentinel indicator
options.D: Adverse event

explanation: Don't worry, clinical terms can be tricky at first! An adverse event simply means harm that happened because of medical treatment, not the disease itself. You've got this!

question: What is another common name for psychiatric parole in mental health care?

options.A: Forced institutionalization
options.B: Conditional release
options.C: Absolute discharge
options.D: Criminal extradition

explanation: Spot on! Psychiatric parole is often called conditional release because patients leave the hospital to continue their recovery under specific medical and legal conditions.

question: As a midwife checking the lower boundary of the pelvic cavity, which bones help form the pelvic outlet?

options.A: Acetabulum and pubic tubercle
options.B: Ischial tuberosities and coccyx
options.C: Linea terminalis and sacral ala
options.D: Iliac crests and sacral promontory

explanation: Think of the bottom exit of the pelvis: it's bounded by your tailbone (coccyx), the sitting bones (ischial tuberosities), and the front pubic bone.

question: Who serves as the vital link between frontline nursing care and software developers?

options.A: Pharmacy technicians
options.B: Hospital billing clerks
options.C: Nurse informaticians
options.D: Biomedical electricians

explanation: Exactly right! Nurse informaticians combine real bedside nursing experience with computer science to help design better healthcare tech.

question: During a massive disaster with limited supplies, how should medical items be shared out?

options.A: Exclusively to patients who arrived first at the emergency department
options.B: Based on objective survival criteria rather than arrival time
options.C: Based on the patient's personal wealth and social status
options.D: Randomly distributed using a lottery system among all injured

explanation: Spot on! We focus on saving the most lives by giving resources to those with the best chance of survival, rather than just who arrived first.

question: What is 'alert fatigue' in a clinical environment?

options.A: Slow loading times when opening multiple patient charts at once
options.B: Physical exhaustion from standing too long at the nursing computer station
options.C: Battery failure in wireless mobile computer carts during a night shift
options.D: Desensitization to warnings caused by too many unimportant pop-up alerts

explanation: Spot on! When software constantly cries wolf with trivial pop-ups, nurses get tired of them and start ignoring all warnings—even the life-saving ones.

question: In which operating theatre zone must staff always wear a surgical mask over their nose and mouth?

options.A: Unrestricted zone
options.B: Semi-restricted zone
options.C: Administrative zone
options.D: Restricted zone

explanation: Masks are a must in the restricted zone, where open wounds and sterile trays are exposed to the environment.

question: What is the approximate time it takes to complete a standard barium swallow procedure?

options.A: Exactly 5 minutes
options.B: 2 to 3 hours
options.C: Over 24 hours
options.D: 15 to 30 minutes

explanation: Most standard barium swallow exams are relatively quick, taking between a quarter to half an hour depending on patient cooperation and findings. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h4)

question: Why do water quality testers measure turbidity?

options.A: To calculate the total mineral salt content in wells
options.B: To measure the exact temperature of the water source
options.C: To determine the amount of dissolved oxygen available
options.D: To check how cloudy the water is from suspended particles

explanation: Great job! Turbidity just means cloudiness. High cloudiness is dangerous because it hides harmful germs from water treatment chemicals.

question: Why does the blood-brain barrier present a major hurdle when treating certain brain infections?

options.A: It actively destroys all types of antibiotics in the blood
options.B: It prevents many helpful medicines from entering brain tissue
options.C: It increases the pressure of cerebrospinal fluid dangerously
options.D: It allows bacteria to hide safely inside the ventricles

explanation: The same tight barriers that keep harmful toxins out also block many beneficial pharmaceutical drugs from reaching infections inside the brain. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h7)

question: A nurse notices pressure sores are common in the elderly ward and tries a new turning schedule. What is this an example of?

options.A: An illegal medical experiment on vulnerable human subjects
options.B: A quality improvement project based on clinical observation
options.C: A violation of hospital administrative policy
options.D: A financial investment in medical equipment manufacturing

explanation: Spot on! Noticing a ward problem and trying a practical nursing fix to make things better is a classic quality improvement project.

question: Why do maternity homes hold clinical audits and review close-calls?

options.A: To find staff members to penalize for minor mistakes
options.B: To increase the cost of antenatal registration fees
options.C: To identify safety gaps and improve future clinical care quality
options.D: To reduce the number of patients seeking care at the facility

explanation: That's right! Audits help the team learn from close-calls so they can make patient care safer for the next mum.

question: What is a primary responsibility of community health nurses regarding food security?

options.A: Inspecting the mechanical engines of commercial cargo vehicles
options.B: Identifying nutritional deficits and educating vulnerable families
options.C: Setting international market prices for agricultural crops
options.D: Driving heavy trucks to transport harvests from farms to cities

explanation: Nurses assess nutritional health at the grassroots level and teach communities how to make the best use of available foods. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h8)

question: What is the name of the layer of cells that clings directly to the released egg upon ovulation?

options.A: Zona pellucida
options.B: Endometrium
options.C: Corona radiata
options.D: Myometrium

explanation: You got it! The corona radiata is a crown-like layer of follicular cells surrounding the egg that incoming sperm have to navigate through.

question: A nurse notices dried blood on a clamp coming out of the washer. What should be done?

options.A: The cleaning process was incomplete and the instrument must be re-washed
options.B: The instrument is permanently stained but still safe to use
options.C: The autoclave cycle reached too high a temperature
options.D: The packaging material was sealed incorrectly

explanation: Spot on! If you still see dirt or blood, the washing stage failed. Any leftover organic matter blocks sterilization, so back to the wash it goes!

question: How does a public health nurse help prevent abuse by starting a support group for young, first-time parents?

options.A: By forcing families to report their income to the government
options.B: By replacing the need for pediatric medical check-ups
options.C: By monitoring parents for illegal drug use in their homes
options.D: By building parenting skills and reducing social isolation

explanation: Connecting young parents with peers and teaching them parenting skills stops the loneliness and frustration that can lead to abuse.

question: Which of these is NOT a factor that helps sustain an endemic disease in a community?

options.A: Low childhood immunization rates
options.B: Universal access to clean water
options.C: Inadequate waste management
options.D: Poor housing construction

explanation: Clean water actually stops diseases from spreading! Poor sanitation and lack of clean water are what help infections stick around.

question: Which common test is used to tell Staphylococcus and Streptococcus apart?

options.A: Acid-fast test
options.B: Gram stain test
options.C: Catalase test
options.D: Capsule staining test

explanation: Great work! Staph makes an enzyme called catalase that bubbles up when you add hydrogen peroxide, but strep doesn't.

question: A patient is admitted with a new multidrug-resistant bacterial infection. What is your most immediate clinical priority as the nurse?

options.A: Implementing appropriate isolation precautions based on transmission route
options.B: Teaching the patient how to perform daily wound dressings
options.C: Scheduling the patient for immediate surgical debridement
options.D: Administering a broad-spectrum antiviral medication

explanation: Safety first! Before anything else, block that bug from spreading to other vulnerable patients by putting the right isolation precautions in place.

question: What is an effective strategy to improve nutritional intake in an older adult with poor appetite?

options.A: Waiting until the patient asks for food once a day
options.B: Serving small, nutrient-dense meals more frequently
options.C: Removing all favorite cultural foods from the diet
options.D: Forcing the patient to finish three large meals daily

explanation: Smaller meals are less overwhelming for seniors with low appetite, and making them nutrient-dense ensures they still get enough calories and vitamins. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h4)

question: A community insists that physical inactivity is not a problem for them at all. As a nurse, what should you do first?

options.A: Launch an intensive gym membership subsidy program
options.B: Close local food markets that sell processed snacks
options.C: Penalize community leaders for refusing to exercise
options.D: Raise awareness and build local recognition of the issue

explanation: Correct! When a community is in denial, jumping straight into action programs won't work. You have to start by building awareness of the issue first.

question: Why do governments create food and nutrition policies?

options.A: To completely ban bringing any foreign food into the country
options.B: To control the exact daily price of goods in local markets
options.C: To manage employment records for all farm workers
options.D: To connect what farmers grow directly with what communities need to stay healthy

explanation: Food policies help make sure that farming output meets the actual nutritional health needs of the population. Great job thinking about the big picture!

question: What must the nurse check or do immediately before pulling back the syringe plunger to create a vacuum?

options.A: Boil the entire plastic syringe in hot water
options.B: Attach a heavy electrical cord to the back handle
options.C: Ensure the vacuum valves or buttons are closed
options.D: Fill the cylinder completely with sterile water

explanation: If the valves are left open while pulling the plunger, air simply enters the syringe from the outside and no vacuum is created. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h3)

question: What happens when you give an opioid antagonist like naloxone?

options.A: It slows down digestion to increase drug absorption.
options.B: It blocks and reverses opioid receptor activity completely.
options.C: It lowers body temperature during a severe fever.
options.D: It stimulates mu receptors to provide deep pain relief.

explanation: Think of naloxone as the ultimate rescue drug. It kicks opioids right off their receptors to instantly reverse dangerous breathing slowdowns.

question: Which group is generally at the highest risk of abuse and neglect in home care settings?

options.A: Young adults recovering from minor sports injuries
options.B: Physically independent middle-aged business executives
options.C: Healthcare professionals working in community clinics
options.D: Frail elderly individuals and those with memory issues

explanation: Spot on! People who are physically frail or have cognitive challenges often depend heavily on others, making them more vulnerable to mistreatment.

question: How do you convert a patient's weight from pounds (lbs) to kilograms (kg)?

options.A: Multiply the weight in pounds by 16
options.B: Divide the weight in pounds by 2.2
options.C: Divide the weight in pounds by 10
options.D: Multiply the weight in pounds by 2.2

explanation: Easy peasy! Since one kilogram is about 2.2 pounds, you just divide the patient's weight in pounds by 2.2 to get kilograms.

question: Why do governments mandate food fortification, like adding iodine to table salt?

options.A: To change the natural color and taste of everyday grocery products
options.B: To prevent common micronutrient deficiency diseases across the population
options.C: To artificially increase the commercial market price of basic food items
options.D: To reduce the total number of calories found in packaged goods

explanation: Fortifying everyday foods helps protect the whole community from sneaky vitamin and mineral deficiencies.

question: Which cranial nerve are you testing when you shine a penlight into a patient's eyes to check their pupils?

options.A: Cranial nerve I
options.B: Cranial nerve XII
options.C: Cranial nerve III
options.D: Cranial nerve VIII

explanation: Cranial nerve III (the oculomotor nerve) handles pupillary constriction. It's a quick reflex test you'll do all the time in clinicals!

question: Which main chemical in tobacco makes it so addictive?

options.A: Ammonia
options.B: Tar
options.C: Carbon monoxide
options.D: Nicotine

explanation: Nicotine is the addictive substance in tobacco that hooks the brain and drives the urge to keep smoking. You've got this!

question: Which sleep disorder involves the upper airway repeatedly collapsing while a person sleeps?

options.A: Primary insomnia
options.B: Obstructive sleep apnea
options.C: Restless legs syndrome
options.D: Narcolepsy

explanation: In obstructive sleep apnea, throat muscles relax too much during sleep and temporarily block airflow, causing the person to briefly wake up to breathe.

question: What is the main goal of disease prevention in public health?

options.A: Finding new surgical methods for complex chronic illnesses
options.B: Stopping health problems before they start or halting their progress
options.C: Reducing the cost of pharmaceutical manufacturing plants
options.D: Increasing hospital admission rates for routine checkups

explanation: You've got this! Prevention is all about stopping illness proactively before it takes hold, rather than just treating symptoms later.

question: What is the main job of Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG) in early pregnancy?

options.A: To signal the corpus luteum to continue producing progesterone
options.B: To lower the mother's blood pressure during the first trimester
options.C: To prepare the fetal lungs for air breathing
options.D: To stimulate milk production in the maternal mammary glands

explanation: Wonderful! hCG is the famous pregnancy hormone that tells the ovary's corpus luteum to keep pumping out progesterone until the placenta is ready to take over.

question: Which element of risk management provides clear, evidence-based rules for clinical practice?

options.A: Patient satisfaction surveys
options.B: Policies and procedures
options.C: Doctor-nurse scheduling
options.D: Financial budgeting

explanation: Written policies give staff clear instructions on the safe way to perform procedures like medication administration or wound care. [learn more](GST319_U4_T6#GST319_U4_T6_h2)

question: What does the abbreviation HAI stand for in nursing practice?

options.A: High acuity illness
options.B: Hygiene assessment indicator
options.C: Healthcare-associated infection
options.D: Hospital antiseptic index

explanation: HAIs are infections patients acquire while receiving medical treatment in a hospital or clinic facility. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h8)

question: What must a unit manager consider when making a fair duty roster?

options.A: Patient acuity and staff skill mix
options.B: The distance of each nurse's house from the hospital
options.C: The personal fashion preferences of nurses
options.D: Only the seniority of the nurses

explanation: Exactly! A good roster looks at how sick the patients are (acuity) and matches them with nurses who have the right skills for the job.

question: What was the purpose of trephining in ancient societies?

options.A: To let trapped evil spirits escape the skull
options.B: To relieve pressure from a physical head injury
options.C: To deliver herbal medicines directly to tissue
options.D: To lower high blood pressure in the brain

explanation: Healers cut holes in the skull believing it created a physical exit door for the demons causing the mental illness. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why is priority setting necessary during community health planning?

options.A: Villagers usually refuse to discuss more than a single topic per meeting
options.B: Diseases always occur in isolation rather than in groups
options.C: Government regulations forbid treating more than one disease at a time
options.D: Resources are limited and not all health problems can be solved at once

explanation: Since funds, staff, and time are always limited, nurses must rank problems to tackle the most urgent ones first. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h3)

question: A patient with severe malaria hesitates to see a doctor because they have no cash. What reform fixes this?

options.A: A policy requiring cash deposits before any nursing assessment
options.B: Increasing taxes on everyday food and household items
options.C: Closing public clinics to save money on utility bills
options.D: Subsidized health insurance schemes that cover treatment costs

explanation: Health insurance steps in so patients can get treated for illnesses like malaria without needing cash right at the hospital door.

question: What biological process mainly causes the sudden height increase (growth spurt) during puberty?

options.A: The stretching of skin cells due to increased daily water intake
options.B: A sudden decrease in physical activity during school hours
options.C: A temporary failure of the pituitary gland to release hormones
options.D: Sex hormones interacting with growth hormone to lengthen bones

explanation: You got it! Rising sex hormones team up with growth hormone to help bones lengthen quickly during the adolescent growth spurt.

question: What is the main difference between a human-made disaster and a natural disaster?

options.A: It always provides weeks of advance warning to the public
options.B: It is triggered by human actions or technical failures
options.C: It never results in mass casualties or physical injuries
options.D: It only occurs inside large industrial manufacturing factories

explanation: You've got this! Human-made disasters happen because of human errors, equipment failures, or negligence, rather than forces of nature like storms or earthquakes.

question: What usually happens shortly after a care-seeking patient gets normal test results from a doctor?

options.A: The anxiety returns and doubt creeps back in
options.B: The patient is permanently cured of all health fears
options.C: The patient stops visiting hospitals for the rest of life
options.D: The patient develops severe physical paralysis

explanation: Medical reassurance rarely lasts long for them. Soon enough, doubt creeps back in, and they start questioning if the lab results were a mistake.

question: What is the main role of the critical care nurse when family and medical teams disagree on life support choices?

options.A: Acting as a patient advocate to uphold their wishes and values
options.B: Directing the family members to leave the unit during discussions
options.C: Making the final legal decision on behalf of the medical team
options.D: Consulting hospital finance departments about treatment costs

explanation: Nurses stand up for the patient's voice, making sure their values and known preferences guide tough care choices.

question: When should you usually give a patient their pain medication before a scheduled dressing change?

options.A: Right after you finish the dressing change
options.B: About 30 minutes before the procedure
options.C: Only if the patient starts crying
options.D: Two hours before so it wears off

explanation: Giving pain meds about half an hour early gives the drug time to kick in right when you start cleaning sensitive tissue. Patient comfort is key!

question: Which channel is best suited for sharing public health findings with local study participants?

options.A: Closed corporate board meetings for hospital executives
options.B: Advanced molecular biology laboratory symposia
options.C: Expensive international subscription-only journals
options.D: Community town halls and local radio broadcasts

explanation: Local forums and media reach ordinary citizens directly in a language they can easily understand. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is the main goal of using the 'teach-back' method after educating a patient?

options.A: To fulfill a legal requirement for signing surgical consent forms
options.B: To allow the nurse to take a break while the patient teaches the class
options.C: To test the patient's long-term memory for academic medical trivia
options.D: To have the patient explain instructions in their own words to verify understanding

explanation: Teach-back isn't testing the patient—it's testing *us*. If they can explain it back easily, you know your teaching hit the mark!

question: What do we mean by 'psychological safety' in a nursing unit?

options.A: The mandatory wearing of protective equipment
options.B: The physical security of staff against outside intruders
options.C: The freedom to speak up about safety concerns without fear
options.D: The absence of stressful patients in the ward

explanation: Exactly! Psychological safety means you can ask questions or report a worry without stressing about being yelled at or victimized by colleagues.

question: What often causes health policies to fail during implementation?

options.A: Medical doctors writing too many discharge summaries
options.B: Too many nurses participating in hospital board meetings
options.C: Patients refusing to take free prescribed medications
options.D: Poor funding, corruption, and lack of political will

explanation: Even great laws on paper fail if leaders do not provide money or commitment to execute them properly. [learn more](GST321_U6_T3#GST321_U6_T3_h7)

question: When assessing a patient with an acquired immune deficiency, what should you look for in their history?

options.A: A family history of rare genetic blood disorders
options.B: Inherited metabolic syndromes from parents
options.C: Childhood developmental milestones and birth weight
options.D: Recent infections, malnutrition, or exposure to certain medications

explanation: You got it! Because acquired deficiencies come from outside triggers like poor nutrition, drugs, or infections, checking their recent history is key.

question: Which of these shows that a health advocacy campaign was truly successful?

options.A: The number of meetings held without reaching any agreement
options.B: A newly passed local health policy or increased service uptake
options.C: Increased complaints from hospital administrative staff
options.D: A reduction in the total number of community volunteers

explanation: Brilliant! Seeing actual policy changes or more people showing up to use health services proves your advocacy hard work paid off.

question: How does administrative informatics differ from clinical nursing informatics?

options.A: It looks at whole hospital systems and units rather than individual bedside care
options.B: It has no connection whatsoever to patient health outcomes
options.C: It is handled exclusively by computer programmers without nursing input
options.D: It only applies to outpatient community health centers in rural areas

explanation: While clinical informatics targets the individual bedside encounter, administrative informatics evaluates broad operational and institutional trends. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T2#GNS113_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why can it be dangerous when two different drugs compete for the exact same CYP450 enzyme?

options.A: It turns every medication into a harmful poison immediately
options.B: It can cause one drug to build up to toxic levels because its breakdown is delayed
options.C: It prevents the stomach from absorbing any water or nutrients
options.D: It instantly stops all blood flow to the kidneys and liver

explanation: Imagine two cars trying to pass through a single-lane toll gate. If the enzymes are busy clearing Drug A, Drug B has to wait in line, builds up in the blood, and can cause toxicity!

question: Who is responsible for making sure the nursing learning environment stays great?

options.A: Just the class reps in first year
options.B: Students, educators, and school administrators together
options.C: Exclusively the hospital medical director
options.D: Only the external licensing board

explanation: Building a wonderful nursing school environment takes teamwork. Everyone—from students to lecturers and management—has a role to play!

question: What did the old FDA pregnancy Category X label mean for a medication?

options.A: No animal testing had been performed on the substance
options.B: Human studies proved the drug cured congenital infections
options.C: Fetal risks clearly outweighed any potential therapeutic benefit
options.D: The drug was completely safe for use at any gestational age

explanation: Category X meant 'Do not use!' The danger to the baby was proven and far outweighed any help the drug could give the mother.

question: What is the correct order for checking a patient's tummy during a physical exam?

options.A: Auscultation, inspection, palpation, percussion
options.B: Percussion, palpation, inspection, auscultation
options.C: Palpation, percussion, auscultation, inspection
options.D: Inspection, auscultation, percussion, palpation

explanation: You listen (auscultation) before you tap or press! If you touch the tummy first, you might change the natural bowel sounds and get a false reading. You've got this!

question: Why do skeletal muscles get bigger when someone does heavy weightlifting regularly?

options.A: Cellular hypertrophy occurs due to increased functional demand
options.B: Metaplasia transforms fat tissue directly into muscle tissue
options.C: Atrophy removes damaged proteins to make space for fluid
options.D: Hyperplasia creates brand new muscle fibers in the tissue

explanation: You're crushing this! Since muscle fibers don't easily make brand new cells, the existing cells bulk up (hypertrophy) to handle the heavy workload.

question: What does 'information asymmetry' mean in the healthcare setting?

options.A: Patients understand treatment options better than hospital administrators
options.B: Medical prices are published openly for everyone in the community to see
options.C: Doctors possess much more medical knowledge than their patients
options.D: Health insurance companies have access to all patient medical records

explanation: It just means an imbalance: the doctor or nurse has years of professional training, while the patient often relies entirely on our guidance to understand what's wrong. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h3)

question: What kind of data do you mainly collect in qualitative research?

options.A: Words, text, and descriptions of human experiences
options.B: Statistical percentages of patient readmissions
options.C: Exact laboratory blood chemistry measurements
options.D: Precise numerical vital signs recorded hourly

explanation: While quantitative loves numbers, qualitative loves words! It looks at interview notes and stories to understand human experiences.

question: What should you do immediately if your patient starts coughing violently and turning blue while you are passing a tube?

options.A: Ask the patient to take a deep breath and swallow
options.B: Push the tube down faster to clear the way
options.C: Stop pushing and pull the tube right back out
options.D: Inject water to wash it down

explanation: Coughing and turning blue (cyanosis) means the tube has mistakenly slipped into the windpipe instead of the food pipe. Pull it back out immediately and let them catch their breath!

question: What is the main goal of Community-Based Rehabilitation (CBR) programs?

options.A: To keep patients admitted in tertiary hospitals for long-term recovery
options.B: To provide acute surgical interventions for physical injuries
options.C: To connect patients with local resources and support for community living
options.D: To isolate individuals with disabilities from the general public

explanation: CBR programs bring rehabilitation and support services directly into the community to help individuals live active, integrated lives. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of priming extension tubing with normal saline before starting an IV?

options.A: To remove trapped air and prevent air embolisms
options.B: To warm the tubing up to body temperature
options.C: To test if the syringe plunger moves smoothly
options.D: To dilute any medication given later on

explanation: Clearing all air bubbles from the line stops air from entering the patient's bloodstream during cannulation. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why is giving just extra cash not always enough to keep healthcare workers in rural posts?

options.A: Government regulations prohibit paying extra allowances to primary health workers
options.B: Rural communities prefer paying traditional healers instead of salaried staff
options.C: Inflation rates immediately render cash allowances completely worthless
options.D: Workers also need decent housing, security, and career growth opportunities

explanation: Money is great, but nurses also care about a safe place to sleep, regular promotions, and opportunities to grow professionally.

question: How would you best describe the peritoneum?

options.A: A thick muscular wall separating the chest and belly
options.B: The outermost layer of the human heart muscle
options.C: The primary filtering unit inside human kidneys
options.D: A serous membrane lining the abdominal cavity

explanation: You've got this! The peritoneum is a smooth, slippery lining that wraps around your tummy wall and internal organs, keeping everything neatly cushioned. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h2)

question: Which set of organs belongs to the internal structures of the male reproductive system?

options.A: Prepuce and glans penis
options.B: Scrotal skin and dartos muscle
options.C: Testes and accessory glands
options.D: Scrotum and penile shaft

explanation: Internal structures include the testes, duct system, and accessory glands, while the scrotum and penis are external. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h1)

question: A clinic is in an area that floods every rainy season. What is the best structural safety step for them?

options.A: Issuing warning pamphlets to patients in the waiting room
options.B: Training nurses on how to swim in fast-moving water
options.C: Buying extra bandages and IV fluids for the pharmacy
options.D: Moving the emergency backup generators to an upper floor

explanation: Brilliant! Elevating power systems protects them from floodwaters so the clinic can keep running.

question: How is a multidisciplinary care plan different from a plan made by just one health worker?

options.A: It removes the need for nursing assessments completely
options.B: It allows the patient to change medical diagnoses at any time
options.C: It combines insights from various fields into one unified set of goals
options.D: It focuses exclusively on hospital discharge procedures

explanation: You're doing great! A team plan blends nursing, social work, and medical insights so every angle of the patient's health is covered.

question: Which international bodies often partner to support Nigeria's family planning supplies?

options.A: World Trade Organization
options.B: OPEC Petroleum Board
options.C: UNFPA and USAID
options.D: International Labour Organization

explanation: Organizations like UNFPA (United Nations Population Fund) and USAID play a massive role in funding and shipping family planning commodities to Nigeria.

question: What determines the overall size of a non-lactating human breast?

options.A: The amount of adipose tissue
options.B: The length of the milk ducts
options.C: The thickness of the skin
options.D: The number of active lobes

explanation: Fatty, or adipose, tissue makes up the bulk of non-lactating breast size, whereas glandular tissue varies less between individuals. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h3)

question: When must a nurse choose soap and water over an alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: When you are in a rush between medication rounds
options.B: Every time you enter a clean patient room
options.C: Before taking the blood pressure of a healthy adult
options.D: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids

explanation: Soap and water physically wash away visible dirt, organic material, and certain tough spores that alcohol rubs cannot destroy effectively. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h4)

question: In public health statistics, what age limit is used to define an orphan?

options.A: Under 5 years of age
options.B: Under 15 years of age
options.C: Under 18 years of age
options.D: Under 21 years of age

explanation: Global health guidelines define an orphan as any child who has lost a parent before reaching their 18th birthday. You've got this!

question: Why can predictive formulas (like the Harris-Benedict equation) sometimes be misleading for critically ill patients?

options.A: They measure direct body heat rather than gas exchange
options.B: They require the patient to be placed inside a sealed heat chamber
options.C: They only provide estimates and may miscalculate actual needs during severe illness
options.D: They can only be used on healthy newborn infants

explanation: Formulas use averages for healthy people. But when a patient has severe burns or trauma, their body behaves unpredictably, so formulas can miss the mark.

question: Which of these is a common sign of psychological trauma in a displaced child?

options.A: An intense desire to learn foreign languages
options.B: Sudden withdrawal, bedwetting, or clingy behavior
options.C: An unexpected increase in academic test scores
options.D: A sudden preference for eating spicy local foods

explanation: Trauma often shows up as regressive behaviors in kids, such as bedwetting, acting extra clingy, or withdrawing from others.

question: What happens during biological magnification (biomagnification) in a food chain?

options.A: Microbiological pathogens are neutralized by natural river currents
options.B: Fish grow larger and healthier due to the presence of mineral nutrients
options.C: Algae populations decrease rapidly due to cold water temperatures
options.D: Toxic chemicals become more concentrated in predators at higher trophic levels

explanation: Correct! As small creatures eat toxins and get eaten by bigger fish and animals, the poison multiplies and gets stronger higher up the food chain.

question: A patient just had cataract surgery and is getting ready to go home. What is a key instruction to give them?

options.A: Wash your face vigorously with antibacterial soap daily
options.B: Sleep flat on your back without using any pillows
options.C: Avoid heavy lifting and straining during bowel movements
options.D: Keep the affected eye uncovered at all times

explanation: Spot on! Straining or heavy lifting ramps up the pressure inside the eye, which is the last thing you want right after eye surgery.

question: Which vaccination is considered a mandatory occupational health requirement for healthcare workers handling clinical waste?

options.A: Hhepatitis B
options.B: Yellow fever only
options.C: Rabies
options.D: Cholera

explanation: Hepatitis B immunization protects clinical personnel from bloodborne viral transmission following occupational exposure incidents. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h9)

question: What do we call the path germs use to leave their reservoir?

options.A: Mode of transmission
options.B: Susceptible host
options.C: Portal of entry
options.D: Portal of exit

explanation: Just like leaving a room through a door, germs use a 'portal of exit' (like coughing or through body fluids) to leave their host.

question: What role do cultural traditions play in nutrition?

options.A: They ensure that every person eats a balanced amount of vitamins
options.B: They prevent communities from consuming processed fast foods
options.C: They dictate the exact financial cost of groceries in a market
options.D: They dictate what foods are considered acceptable and how meals are prepared

explanation: Culture shapes food preferences, cooking methods, and the social significance attached to eating together. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T020#GNS227_U2_T020_h5)

question: What is the primary medication used to treat intestinal tapeworm infections?

options.A: Paracetamol
options.B: Amoxicillin
options.C: Praziquantel
options.D: Chloroquine

explanation: Spot on! Praziquantel is the go-to drug that stuns and paralyzes the tapeworm so the body can pass it out safely.

question: What happens to bacteria when food is placed inside a properly working freezer?

options.A: They are instantly and fully killed.
options.B: Their reproduction stops completely.
options.C: They multiply faster in the cold air.
options.D: They turn into spores and fly away.

explanation: Freezing puts bacteria to sleep (dormant state), stopping them from multiplying, but it doesn't kill them completely.

question: Which of these is an example of a non-clinical outsourced hospital service?

options.A: Administering intravenous medications
options.B: Hospital laundry and facility maintenance
options.C: Specialized renal dialysis procedures
options.D: Diagnostic laboratory blood testing

explanation: Things like cleaning, washing linens, and security are support services that don't involve direct medical treatment, making them great for outsourcing.

question: A community nurse notices that three children from the same household missed their measles vaccines. Which record system helped reveal this?

options.A: Monthly financial summary
options.B: Family folder
options.C: Staff attendance register
options.D: National drug ledger

explanation: Wonderful! Because family folders group household members together, it's easy for nurses to spot patterns and catch missed vaccines across siblings.

question: What exactly is a 'prodrug'?

options.A: A vitamin supplement taken before meals to enhance drug absorption
options.B: A chemical that completely blocks liver enzymes from working
options.C: An old medication that has been replaced by newer pharmaceutical formulations
options.D: A medication administered in an inactive form that relies on metabolism to become active

explanation: A prodrug is like a secret agent! It is given in an inactive form and relies on your body's metabolic processes to switch it 'on' so it can do its therapeutic job.

question: What is an effective community nursing strategy to help stop FGM?

options.A: Inspecting every household's private rooms every single week
options.B: Punishing mothers publicly for crimes committed by elders
options.C: Banning all community meetings and traditional gatherings in villages
options.D: Promoting alternative rites of passage that celebrate maturity without cutting

explanation: Spot on! Offering safe, positive ways to celebrate cultural milestones helps communities keep their traditions alive while dropping the dangerous cutting.

question: Which of these commonly causes frustration when using mobile nursing technology on the ward?

options.A: Too many physical stairs in modern multi-story hospitals
options.B: Dead batteries and poor wireless internet connectivity
options.C: Patients demanding to program the IV pumps themselves
options.D: Doctors refusing to let nurses touch computer carts

explanation: So true! Nothing slows down a shift quite like a dying battery or a spinning loading wheel when you're trying to chart quickly.

question: As a community health nurse, what is one of your key responsibilities regarding social services?

options.A: Drafting new national legislation for disability rights in parliament
options.B: Connecting patients and families with appropriate community resources and referrals
options.C: Managing government financial budgets for social welfare departments
options.D: Constructing physical ramps and elevators in public buildings

explanation: Nurses act as wonderful bridge-builders! You spot patient needs and point them toward the correct social support agencies.

question: Why can the withdrawal method fail to prevent pregnancy even when the man pulls out on time?

options.A: Pre-ejaculatory fluid may contain active sperm
options.B: Urine mixes with semen inside the bladder
options.C: Semen can absorb through the skin of the thigh
options.D: Vaginal walls produce their own sperm cells

explanation: Pre-cum released during excitement can pick up leftover sperm waiting in the urethra, introducing them into the vagina before the actual pull-out.

question: A patient experiences heavy monthly bleeding and cramping as the inner lining of her uterus sheds. Which layer is primarily involved?

options.A: Myometrium
options.B: Endometrium
options.C: Cervical stroma
options.D: Perimetrium

explanation: The endometrium is the inner mucosal lining that builds up and sheds every month during menstruation. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h3)

question: What is the main difference between a research question and a hypothesis?

options.A: A hypothesis is used only in qualitative studies
options.B: A research question is always written after data collection
options.C: A hypothesis never mentions variables or patient populations
options.D: A research question asks an inquiry, while a hypothesis makes a predicted statement

explanation: Simple rule: a research question asks a question ('Does X affect Y?'), while a hypothesis makes an educated guess at the answer ('X will increase Y').

question: Which part of the nail is responsible for growing new nail cells?

options.A: The nail plate
options.B: The nail matrix
options.C: The cuticle
options.D: The nail bed

explanation: Great job! The nail matrix sits right under the skin at the base and does all the hard work of making new cells that push forward to form your hard nails.

question: What is a major health risk in overcrowded refugee or displaced persons (IDP) camps?

options.A: A sudden surplus of safe drinking water
options.B: Complete elimination of nutritional deficiencies
options.C: Immediate eradication of chronic lifestyle illnesses
options.D: Rapid outbreaks of waterborne and communicable diseases

explanation: Well done! When people live close together with poor sanitation, infections like cholera and measles can spread very quickly.

question: A patient with a complex heart condition requiring open-heart surgery should be sent to which level of care?

options.A: Primary health post
options.B: Maternity home care
options.C: Patent medicine store
options.D: Tertiary health care

explanation: Tertiary facilities like teaching hospitals have the advanced equipment and specialists required for complex surgeries. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of doing a Root Cause Analysis after a mistake happens?

options.A: To find a way to hide the mistake from hospital administrators
options.B: To calculate the exact financial cost of the patient injury
options.C: To determine which single staff member should be fired
options.D: To uncover underlying system flaws that allowed the error to happen

explanation: Correct! Root cause analysis isn't about finger-pointing; it digs into the system to fix the real problem so it never happens again.

question: Why does Primary Health Care require different sectors to work together (intersectoral collaboration)?

options.A: Because the Ministry of Health cannot legally purchase medications without other ministries
options.B: Because doctors need assistance from foreign engineers to run rural clinics
options.C: Because health is influenced by non-medical factors like education, agriculture, and clean water
options.D: Because nurses are required to work in agricultural fields during planting seasons

explanation: Well done! Good health goes beyond medicine. It relies heavily on food security, safe water, and education—which means different government sectors must team up.

question: A diabetic patient asks why a tiny blister on their toe is such a big deal. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Small blisters automatically mean the patient is severely dehydrated and needs intravenous fluids
options.B: Poor circulation and nerve damage in diabetes make small sores slow to heal and prone to severe ulcers
options.C: Blisters on the feet are a normal sign that the skin is growing thicker and healthier
options.D: Diabetic patients always have an overactive immune system that destroys normal skin cells

explanation: You nailed it! Because diabetes affects blood flow and nerve feeling, a tiny foot sore can easily hide and turn into a dangerous ulcer if we aren't careful.

question: Why do civil lawsuits often name both the nurse and the hospital as defendants?

options.A: Because the hospital shares responsibility for employee actions under institutional liability
options.B: Because hospitals commit more medication errors than individual nurses
options.C: Because nursing councils require hospitals to pay all court fines
options.D: To ensure the nurse does not have to pay any legal fees

explanation: Hospitals usually share the blame (and liability) for mistakes made by their staff during working hours.

question: Which of these is a great example of community-level disaster prep?

options.A: Clearing blocked drainage channels together before the rainy season begins
options.B: Relying entirely on federal radio broadcasts for weather updates
options.C: Waiting inside a flooded home for international rescue helicopters
options.D: Reporting abandoned buildings only after they collapse

explanation: Brilliant! Clearing drains together is a practical grassroots action that stops floods before the heavy rains even start.

question: Why is it important for a nurse manager to understand their hospital's chain of command?

options.A: To ensure that nurses never participate in patient care decisions
options.B: To guarantee that the hospital operates as a simple structure
options.C: To avoid having to communicate with any physicians or doctors
options.D: To effectively navigate reporting lines and advocate for resources

explanation: Knowing who to talk to up the ladder helps nurse managers solve problems quickly, speak up for their ward, and get needed supplies.

question: A nurse checks a client's chart to see if their symptoms have lasted long enough to meet clinical guidelines. Which manual is she likely using?

options.A: The DSM-5-TR
options.B: The International Nursing Index
options.C: The Hospital Safety Manual
options.D: The British Pharmacopoeia

explanation: The DSM-5-TR gives exact timelines and severity checklists that clinicians use to match a client's symptoms. You're mastering psychiatric tools!

question: What should a nurse do immediately after spotting a suspected Category 1 infectious disease?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately to prevent hospital overcrowding
options.B: Wait until the end of the month to compile all clinic registers
options.C: Post the patient's details on social media to warn the public
options.D: Isolate the patient and notify the facility surveillance officer

explanation: You got it! Isolate the patient right away to keep others safe, then alert the surveillance officer to kick off the reporting chain.

question: A patient who had a barium enema yesterday hasn't passed any stool yet and now has worsening belly pain. What should you do?

options.A: Tell them to wait another three days before worrying
options.B: Notify the doctor right away, because trapped barium can cause a serious blockage
options.C: Reassure them that white stools take a whole week to clear
options.D: Advise them to eat a heavy meal to push the stool down

explanation: If barium gets stuck and the patient has belly pain, it can lead to a bowel impaction or blockage. Quick reporting keeps the patient safe!

question: Why is regular monitoring of maternal blood pressure important during labor?

options.A: To detect pregnancy-induced hypertension or shock early
options.B: To calculate the exact birth weight of the baby
options.C: To determine when the placenta will separate
options.D: To measure how fast the cervix is opening

explanation: Tracking maternal blood pressure helps identify dangerous spikes like preeclampsia or drops indicating bleeding or distress. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h4)
